source.title: Crossbow: Scaling Deep Learning with Small Batch Sizes on Multi-GPU Servers
source.authors: Alexandros Koliousis; Pijika Watcharapichat; M. Weidlich; Luo Mai; Paolo Costa; P. Pietzuch

record.file_problem: Full text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies batch size and reports epochs needed to reach a fixed test-accuracy target, a different measure of the batch-size effect in V5.
record.gate_note: Figure 3 and its accompanying text report TensorFlow's epochs to reach 80% test accuracy across batch sizes. Other batch-size and learner comparisons focus on time-to-accuracy or throughput, not the fixed-epoch generalization gap in the claim.
record.test_reason: The study uses the large-batch statistical-efficiency penalty to motivate Crossbow. Its batch-size sweep measures epochs to a target test accuracy, without reporting held-out performance under a common fixed epoch budget as V5 specifies. Its remaining comparisons evaluate training-system performance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that Crossbow combines small batches, multiple replicas per GPU, automatic learner-count tuning and synchronous model averaging to improve hardware efficiency with low loss of statistical efficiency, shortening time-to-accuracy by up to fourfold relative to TensorFlow.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates a multi-GPU training system and compares it with TensorFlow; it does not reproduce the original studies' fixed-epoch generalization-gap measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes the epochs required to reach the test-accuracy target; the paper also reports that the best learner count depends on GPU count and model.

fits_no_version.finding: For TensorFlow ResNet-32 on CIFAR-10, increasing batch size from the tested range of 64–1024 increases epochs needed to reach 80% test accuracy; §2.4 describes super-linear growth beyond approximately 256.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger batches can reduce statistical efficiency, measured as epochs required to reach a fixed held-out accuracy target.

record.problems: The batch-size trend in Figure 3 is not accompanied by precise values in the text or reported uncertainty. The experiment measures epochs to a target test accuracy, rather than test error at a fixed epoch budget.
record.rows_left_out: Other batch-size results focus on time-to-accuracy or throughput and do not measure the fixed-epoch performance named in V5. Learner-count comparisons at fixed batch size likewise do not test the batch-size condition.

untested.parts: Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under a common fixed epoch budget, and whether recipe adaptations remove that penalty.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Longer time in epochs to reach a target accuracy is relevant background for V5, but does not by itself establish the specified fixed-budget comparison. Crossbow's learner-count and synchronization experiments also change the training algorithm rather than isolate that comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and natural-label generalization.
Width beyond interpolation and test error.
The paper reports epochs to a target test accuracy, not test performance at a fixed epoch budget; its reported sweep is for ResNet-32 with TensorFlow.
Sharpness or other measured network properties tracking the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-32 with TensorFlow
rows.operation_detail: Varied images processed per update and measured epochs to reach 80% test accuracy.
rows.note: The text says that as batch size increases, TensorFlow requires more epochs to converge; precise per-size values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: The reported increase in epochs to 80% test accuracy is supported by §2.4, but does not directly measure V5's fixed-epoch accuracy penalty. Retain this as a statistical-efficiency finding, with CIFAR-10 added to the condition. Exact per-batch values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
